content.title: About
content.content: Snow crab (Chionoecetes opilio) is a marine crustacean from cold northern seas. This product contains only the crab legs, flash‑frozen after harvest to preserve freshness, flavor, and texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Crab legs are prized for their sweet, tender meat with a subtle oceanic taste.
The crabs are harvested in the Barents and Bering Seas, where the water is cold and pristine.
Quick‑freeze (IQF) technology retains up to 90 % of nutrients and the natural pink color of the meat.
Snow crab is an important fishery resource for Alaskan and Canadian coastal communities.
Leg meat is rich in protein, omega‑3 fatty acids, and minerals such as zinc and selenium.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Crab leg meat provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: EPA and DHA support heart health, vascular function, and brain performance.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Zinc, selenium and iodine contribute to a healthy immune system and thyroid function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Crab legs contain very little fat, making them suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B12 and B6 aid energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Processing may involve added salt; people with hypertension should monitor total sodium intake.

items.title: Potential contaminants
items.content: Crabs can accumulate heavy metals in polluted waters; choose products from reputable sources.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improper storage after thawing can allow bacterial growth. Follow storage guidelines.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Crab legs can be steamed, boiled, grilled, or baked. They are often served with melted butter, lemon wedges, or a tartar sauce. Before cooking, quickly thaw in the refrigerator or under cold running water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen crab legs at –18 °C or lower in an airtight package. Once thawed, use within 1–2 days and store in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C.
